learning_objective: 🏛️ Discover how power is divided between the central government and states to keep a massive, diverse country like India running smoothly!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: संघवाद (सत्ता का केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के बीच बँटवारा)
अधिकार क्षेत्र (वह कानूनी दायरा जिसके भीतर किसी को निर्णय लेने का अधिकार है)
विकेंद्रीकरण (केंद्र और राज्य से शक्तियां लेकर स्थानीय सरकार को देना)
एकात्मक प्रणाली (जहाँ केवल एक ही स्तर की सरकार होती है या बाकी इकाइयां उसके अधीन होती हैं)
गठबंधन सरकार (जब कोई एक पार्टी बहुमत नहीं पाती, तो कई पार्टियां मिलकर सरकार बनाती हैं)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Federalism is a system of government where power is divided between a central authority and its constituent units (states/provinces). Both levels of government enjoy their power independently of the other.

'Coming Together' federations (like the USA) happen when independent states join together to form a bigger unit. 'Holding Together' federations (like India and Spain) happen when a large country decides to divide its power between the national and state governments.

main_concepts.concept_title: 📜 What makes India a Federal Country?
main_concepts.simple_explanation: The Constitution clearly divides powers into three lists: 1. Union List (defense, foreign affairs - Center decides), 2. State List (police, agriculture - State decides), 3. Concurrent List (education, forests - both can decide, but Center wins in a conflict).

India created states based on languages (like Gujarat for Gujaratis) which actually united the country instead of breaking it. India also has no 'National Language'. Hindi is the official language, alongside 21 other recognized scheduled languages.

A major step was taken in 1992 to make the 3rd tier of democracy (Panchayats and Municipalities) powerful. It made regular elections mandatory, reserved 1/3rd seats for women, and created State Election Commissions.

fun_activity.title: 🏠 Family Federalism
fun_activity.instructions: Think of your house as a country. 'Defense' (locking doors at night) and 'Foreign Affairs' (dealing with neighbors) is handled by the Central Govt (Parents). 'Room Decoration' is handled by the State Govt (You). If your parents try to paint your room without asking, that's a violation of federal jurisdiction!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize at least 3 subjects from each of the Union, State, and Concurrent lists.
📌 The 1992 Decentralisation Act features are highly important (especially the reservation of 1/3 seats for women).
📌 Explain what happens to 'Residuary Subjects' (like computer software that came after the constitution was made) - they fall under the Union Government's control.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Supreme Court acts as an umpire if disputes arise between different levels of government in the exercise of their powers.
⭐ India is a 'Holding Together' federation, which means the central government tends to be more powerful than the states.
⭐ The head of a Gram Panchayat is the Sarpanch, and the head of a Municipal Corporation is the Mayor.
